readerQuestion: How do I use a Home Assistant automation blueprint, change it for my home, and update it without unexpectedly changing every routine that depends on it?
directAnswer: Use a blueprint when its offered inputs match the household rule. Create a configured automation and test one nonessential lamp with real sensor transitions. Edit inputs for ordinary changes; Take control detaches one automation for custom logic. Re-import replaces the common definition, so preserve the old file and inputs, review all dependent automations, and verify them individually after the update.
originalContribution: Sections 3 and 4 contain an input worksheet and four-row acceptance/troubleshooting table for a one-lamp practice routine. The hypothetical 10:00:00 detection, 10:00:45 clear and 10:01:15 turn-off example separates sensor hold time from the configured 30-second delay. Sections 5 and 6 apply blueprint inheritance to a study exception versus five unchanged rooms and explain why disabling a dependent automation does not isolate a shared definition update.
limitations: Documentation and release-tagged source research, not a hardware test or human/expert review. No Home Assistant instance was configured, no real motion timing was measured, and no blueprint update/rollback was executed on a household installation. The checked source is Home Assistant 2026.10.1; an installed or development-branch blueprint may differ. The basic motion example lacks darkness, brightness and manual-override inputs and does not restore an interrupted wait. The image is generated editorial art, not an installation photograph. Verification covers the local website draft, not publication or indexing.
proofreadFixes: The final automated grandma-proofread pass replaced the vague instruction to retain a blueprint file with the Edit in YAML path lookup, an explanation of YAML as text configuration, the blueprints/automation directory, an explicit existing-file-access prerequisite and a defer-if-unavailable instruction. Added a scoped undo procedure that restores the saved definition and any changed inputs before reloading and rechecking. Added a separate sideways-swipe cue immediately above the second wide table. Rechecked the release source to confirm occupancy as well as motion selection, clear-state timing, restart-on-new-detection behavior, and absence of daylight/manual override. Confirmed the four TLDR bullets answer the question directly, the first body section distinguishes an imported definition from a saved automation, source labels are professional, and authorship/research disclosure do not imply testing. Screenshots were retaken after image decoding to avoid recording an incomplete paint as a broken image. Repeated the proofread after these edits: PASS.

claimChecks.claim: Import makes a blueprint available; Create automation with configured inputs creates the runnable routine. Supported import sources include the community forum, GitHub and GitHub Gists.
Blueprint-based automations have independent inputs but inherit changes to their shared definition when reloaded. Disabling an automation does not give it a separate definition.
Take control converts the configured blueprint automation into a regular automation, removes its blueprint inheritance, and has no automatic conversion back.

The 2026.10.1 built-in motion-light blueprint selects motion or occupancy binary sensors and light targets; it triggers off-to-on, waits on-to-off, then applies the configured delay before Off. It has no darkness, brightness or manual-override input. Source read directly from the matching raw release tag as well as checking the public source link.
Restart mode stops the previous action sequence and starts a new one; the worked repeat-detection check is scoped to a new clear-to-detected transition, not continuous detected state.
Run actions skips normal triggers and top-level conditions. The guide instead asks for real motion transitions plus trace inspection and a visible physical result.
A running wait or delay is lost when Home Assistant restarts. The example is not described as restoring its countdown; it links to the established timer-recovery guide.
Minimum Home Assistant versions and required/defaulted inputs belong to the blueprint configuration; imported content can be incompatible with the installed release.
Selector filters can restrict offered entities by domain, device class and integration. A missing picker choice is not alone evidence that the physical device needs re-pairing.
Re-import downloads and replaces a local blueprint rather than guaranteeing automatic tracking of every author change; the historical release description was checked against current instructions.

Automation blueprint files are stored under the configuration directory's blueprints/automation folder; the path under use_blueprint selects the definition, and reload applies file changes. The file-preservation and scoped undo instructions follow this documented mechanism, not a claim of tested recovery.

incomingLinkOpportunities.section: Do I need HACS to use Home Assistant?
incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: A reader checking whether an extra download is necessary can follow a practical example that uses built-in blueprint support and distinguishes blueprint-specific prerequisites.

incomingLinkOpportunities.section: Keep the boundaries clear as you add more routines
incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: After learning what an automation does, a reader repeating the same pattern across rooms can learn when a shared blueprint is appropriate and how updates affect those copies.
